Cut from slide 3 (full wording):
- An agent loop with no stop condition keeps spending on the model provider's account, and it leaves open who is responsible for what the agent did.
- A language model has no persistent state, no ground truth, and no accountability. The loop is the first structure a designer puts around the model, and the loop inherits all three gaps unless the design closes each one: a budget closes the state gap, an observation closes the ground-truth gap, and a ledger closes the accountability gap.
- The design claim Sortie 1 will try to disprove / The loop halts on every input class (answerable, unanswerable, adversarial) within budget, and every turn is in the ledger. If a single run exceeds the turn budget, halts with no ledger event, or produces a 'final answer' without a reasoning turn, the design claim is false.

Cut from slide 4 (full wording):
- In chain-of-thought prompting the model reasons and then answers, and nothing checks the reasoning against the world. /  / ReAct adds the observation. After each action the environment answers back, and the next reasoning step has ground truth in it. /  / This course uses the observation inside the loop as the line between a generative system and an agent: an agent's next reasoning step depends on what the environment returned.
- Chain-of-thought (Wei et al., 2022) / 'Let's think step by step.' The model emits its reasoning as text a person can read, and planning that was latent becomes visible.

Cut from slide 6 (full wording):
- The loop parses each model output into Step, a Pydantic model with the fields kind ∈ {answer, tool}, name, args, and text. A malformed decision cannot reach the loop: the parser rejects it, and the rejection goes back to the model as an observation.
- Final answer · turn budget · cost budget · error. The loop writes each halt to the ledger with its reason, so the Chase can tell a correct halt from an exit that left no record.
- Run the same loop against a hosted API and against Ollama's endpoint. For each run, measure latency, cost, and whether the small model can produce the schema at all.

- Rule for the semester: code enforces every budget, because the model can argue its way past a budget that exists only in the prompt. Halts live in code and in the ledger, never only in the prompt.
7:
Cut from slide 8 (full wording):
- The loop with goals and no grounding, no budget, no evaluator: why it spiraled
- AutoGPT stated the ambition plainly: give a model a goal and let it run. The repository gathered hundreds of thousands of GitHub stars in weeks. /  / Its users also published a shared record of failures: loops that spent budget on the same task, rewrote plans in circles, and reported progress that had not happened. /  / The 2024–25 designs this course covers (evaluators, budgets, human-in-the-loop, workflows over agents) each answer a failure from that spring. /  / Judgment loop: decision = full autonomy from a goal; privileged = ambition and demo value; cost = grounding; failure mode = spiral; preservation = none (by design).
- Which of the nine components was absent, and which absence caused the spiral? / Evaluation: nothing checked a task's result before it fed the next plan; the model graded itself from its own summary. / Governance: the goal was one sentence; no performance measure (PEAS's P), no halt, no attestation. / Memory: a vector store of its own outputs, so the agent retrieved its own hallucinated 'facts' as truth. / Planning was present and fluent. Because nothing grounded the plans, each new plan read well while the task made no progress.

Cut from slide 9 (full wording):
- Same loop, one year apart: what changed, and what was missing in both
- ReAct's authors built it to show that reasoning and acting improve each other, and they evaluated it against benchmarks and nothing else. AutoGPT's developers built it to show that a goal alone can drive a loop, and they gave it no grounding. /  / Both lacked a budget, an evaluator, and a record. gzkit, the system on the next slide, was started in January 2026 to close that gap, after two more years of the same failure.

- The founding exchange (2026-01-12) / The model: for maximizing 'Claudishness,' only specification matters. / The operator: specification, methodology, and governance (all three, or the loop drifts). /  / [Quote from genesis.md — verify wording against the source before class.]
- The operator's remedy changed the documents around the model call and left the call itself alone: a PRD that says WHAT before any HOW, an ADR that records the decision and its alternatives, a brief with allowed paths, and an append-only ledger in which every turn, gate, and attestation is an event. gzkit treats governance as one of the agent's components (the one ReAct and AutoGPT lacked), so the ledger and the gates sit inside the loop.
